items.title: [2611.01386] Learning by Doing: Autonomously Compiling and Curating Agent Skills from Verified Traces
items.summary: A production service called Zep Agent Skills provides procedural memory to deployed LLM agents using only verified task attempts as evidence. A compiler with Reflector and Curator roles transforms these verified traces into versioned Skills, governed by admission gates. The system uses these Skills, which are open standard, for agents to retrieve knowledge through lexical search. Compiling skills from a teacher model significantly increases the pass rate of weaker executor models on tasks. This approach demonstrates substantial gains in performance without requiring continuous fine-tuning.
items.audio_script: From arxiv.org, "[2611.01386] Learning by Doing: Autonomously Compiling and Curating Agent Skills from Verified Traces" details a production service for procedural memory in deployed large language model agents achieved through the compilation and curation of verified task attempts into versioned skills. The system employs a compiler with Reflector and Curator roles to transform these traces into open standard skills governed by admission gates, enabling agents to retrieve knowledge via lexical search. Compiling skills from a teacher model was shown to significantly increase the pass rate of weaker executor models on tasks, demonstrating substantial performance gains without the need for continuous fine-tuning. This research indicates a novel method for autonomous skill acquisition and transfer in artificial intelligence systems.
